notice: SYNTHETIC CORPUS. These messages were written for this project. The organisations, people, sender domains and IP addresses are fictional or reserved for documentation (RFC 2606 / RFC 5737). The only real domains are the brand domains paypal.com, amazon.com and aws.amazon.com, used as the legitimate side of look-alike and must-not-flag tests (nothing is ever fetched). Attachments are inert text stubs with magic bytes only. Nothing here is a real threat sample.

messages.label: benign
messages.description: Marketing newsletter through an ESP: Return-Path and tracking links on the ESP domain, DKIM aligned.

messages.label: benign
messages.description: Internal mail from the real CFO address (a protected name) about invoice approvals: protected name on the real domain must not trigger spoofing.

messages.label: benign
messages.description: Urgent-sounding HR deadline notice, same-domain link, authenticated: urgency alone must stay below the threshold.

messages.label: benign
messages.description: A genuine, user-requested password reset from a SaaS vendor: credential wording and a link to the sender's own domain.

messages.label: benign
messages.description: Order confirmation with a clean PDF invoice attached.

messages.label: benign
messages.description: Automated monitoring alert with no Message-ID header (some scripts omit it); everything else is clean.

messages.label: benign
messages.description: Legitimate internationalised domain (single-script Latin with umlaut, punycode on the wire): must not be reported as a homograph.

messages.label: benign
messages.description: Event ticket with a QR image and 'scan this code at the door' wording. QR wording is weak evidence on its own.

messages.label: benign
messages.description: Courier tracking mail using a URL shortener (stand-in short.test): shortener alone is a minor signal.

messages.label: benign
messages.description: Mailing-list post: Reply-To, Return-Path and Message-ID all belong to the list, not the author's domain.

messages.label: benign
messages.description: Internal security-awareness mail that QUOTES a defanged phishing URL as a teaching example. A static scanner cannot know it is quoted, so it over-scores this message; kept as an honest failure case.

messages.label: suspicious
messages.description: Authenticated partner mail with a password-protected ZIP and the password in the body. Legitimate in practice, but exactly how malware evades gateways.

messages.label: suspicious
messages.description: Unauthenticated 'shared document' notice from an unknown sender, shortened link and sign-in wording.

messages.label: suspicious
messages.description: Invoice notice from an unknown vendor whose Reply-To goes elsewhere; no authentication results.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: Classic brand phish: look-alike sender domain (paypa1), brand display name, text/href mismatch, failing SPF/DMARC.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: Link to an internationalised domain that swaps Latin letters for Cyrillic lookalikes (xn--...), mailbox-full lure.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: 'Signed document' HTML attachment that is really a credential-harvesting form posting to an external host.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: HTML attachment that assembles a download in the browser (Blob + atob + click): HTML smuggling.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: Executable disguised as a PDF with a double extension; magic bytes say MZ.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: Macro-enabled Word document (.docm containing vbaProject.bin) sent as a purchase order.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: Unencrypted ZIP whose only real content is a .pdf.scr screensaver executable.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: Password-protected ZIP holding an executable, password given in the message body to dodge scanners.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: CEO impersonation from a free-mail address asking staff to buy gift cards and keep it quiet.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: CFO impersonation from a one-letter-off look-alike of the company domain, urgent wire to 'new bank details', SPF fails in the offline evaluator, and a Received chain whose timestamps go backwards.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: Spoofed IT Help Desk: password-expiry scare with a link to a domain that embeds the company name.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: 'Re-authenticate MFA' lure delivered as a QR image with no clickable link, from a spoofed brand name.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: Order-problem lure whose link uses the '@' userinfo trick and an obfuscated (hex) IP address as the real host.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: Billing-failure lure whose link bounces through an open-redirect style parameter to a look-alike login host.

messages.label: benign
messages.description: SaaS invoice mail through an ESP: tracking links, invoice wording, DKIM aligned, SPF aligned only to the ESP.

messages.label: benign
messages.description: Newsletter with Greek and accented text and a legitimate accented-Latin domain (café.example); generic greeting only.

messages.label: benign
messages.description: IT Help Desk (real domain) announcing maintenance with a sign-in reminder; protected display name on the real domain.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: 'Payroll' display name from a free-mail account asking to update direct deposit details via a shortened link.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: 'Voice message' lure with an SVG attachment containing script, sender authentication failing.

messages.label: phishing
messages.description: Postal-service fee lure with a decimal-encoded IP host and a brand display name from an unrelated domain.
